subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Sludge: Friction That Hinders
description: A quick, practical guide to Sludge: Friction That Hinders.

hook.text: A veteran applies for benefits. The form is 20 pages, requires three IDs, and has a 45-day wait. Many give up.

buildup.text: Sludge is excessive friction that prevents people from accessing benefits or exercising rights.

discovery.text: Sunstein coined sludge to describe deliberate or negligent obstacles in bureaucratic processes that discourage.

twist.text: Some sludge is intentional. Making it hard to claim rebates or cancel subscriptions saves organizations money.

climax.text: Sludge audits identify and remove unnecessary friction. Governments should make accessing rights as easy as paying.

punchline.text: If the process is hard, ask who benefits from the friction.

quiz.question: What is sludge in behavioral policy?
options: Excessive friction that prevents people from accessing benefits or rights
A nudge that encourages healthy behavior
